we have shown that the use of a multiple problem decomposition in time constrained planning problems, in conjunction with a novel approach to resource allocation, is a viable approach for the efficient synthesis of multiple plans.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the ability to decompose a problem into a collection of subproblems, each of which is solved independently, is not sufficient to guarantee an efficient and effective solution to a multi-agent planning problem.
, in time constrained planning domains, a problem decomposition that allows the planner to reason about both the agent and resource perspectives is necessary to achieve optimal plans.
